fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Matching Quiz
fields.features_subheading: A matching quiz pairs each term with its partner. Emergent builds the quiz, its scoring, and a table of every pair picked.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written from your pairs

Paste each term with its partner, and Emergent writes one question per term, with the right partner and three wrong ones drawn from the same list. Prompt again to change any pair.
fields.feature_2:
The wrong partner, saved with the answer

Every answer is saved with the partner the person picked, not just right or wrong. Sort the table by pair and you see which two terms a class confuses, such as affect and effect.
fields.feature_3:
Pictures in place of words

Ask for a picture on each question, and the quiz shows it one per screen on a phone or tablet. A first grader matches a drawing of a cat to its word without reading a long list.
fields.feature_4:
A fresh answer order for each person

The quiz shuffles the answer choices for each person who opens it. The right partner never sits in the same spot twice, and two students at one table see a different order.
fields.feature_5:
A pass mark, with retakes and alerts

Set a pass mark, such as 10 of 12, and anyone under it is emailed a link to try again. The teacher or manager gets a Slack message or an email that lists who is still under the mark.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and the code in GitHub

Host the quiz on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep the quiz after the term ends.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Groups Run a Matching Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
17 of 52 students swapped affect with effect

Each Friday, Odell Prentiss's 52 students in 2 English classes at Halsey Brook Middle School match 12 words to their meanings. The app saves the meaning each one picked. This week, 17 of 52 gave affect the meaning of effect, more than any other mix-up, and that pair opens Monday's lesson.
fields.tab_content_2:
3 misses put a first grader in Tuesday's group

Tamsin Lowery's 23 first graders at Saltmarsh Elementary match 8 pictures to sight words on classroom tablets, one picture per screen. The app counts the misses for each child. Anyone with 3 or more joins her Tuesday reading group, and this week 6 of 23 did.
fields.tab_content_3:
A retake link goes to any rep under 10 of 12

New sales reps at Wrenmoor Software match 12 product features to the plan that includes each one. A rep who scores under 10 of 12 gets a retake link by email, and sales manager Vesna Albright sees every score in one table. Of the 14 reps hired in October, 11 passed on the first try.
fields.tab_content_4:
On 13 of 15 matches, Corliss Hale wins the party

Before the December party, 34 people at Brindle Lane Architects each sent in one fact about themselves. The quiz asked players to match 15 coworkers to their facts on a phone. The leaderboard ran on the office TV, and Corliss Hale won with 13 of 15.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Matching Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan pairs that test real knowledge, then build them in a matching quiz maker that shows which pairs get confused.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Keep each set to one topic
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the pairs before the questions
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Take wrong choices from the same list
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Decide what counts as a pass
fields.howto_step_1_des: Build each set around one topic, such as this week's vocabulary or one product line. A mixed set lets people match by elimination instead of by knowing. Put the topic and the audience in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the set around them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List every term with its one correct partner before you write a single question. Check that no partner fits two terms, since a second fit marks a right answer wrong. A set of 8 to 12 pairs fits in one sitting.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Use the other partners in the set as the wrong choices. Every option then looks plausible, while a choice of a different kind stands out and gives the answer away. Three wrong choices per question keep each screen short enough to read.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Set the pass mark before anyone plays, such as 10 of 12 for staff training, or skip it for a party game. Then decide what a miss triggers, such as a retake or a review group, and write both rules into the prompt.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Take the quiz yourself, then ask 3 people from the real audience to take it. A pair that all 3 miss can mean two partners overlap rather than a hard term. Fix the wording by prompt before the full group sees it.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the quiz link by email or put it on a class or team page. Each question shows on its own screen, and a phone works as well as a laptop. Every answer lands in the same table, whichever device it came from.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the mix-ups, then reuse the set
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sort the saved answers by pair and look at the partner people picked by mistake. A word given its neighbor's meaning needs a side-by-side lesson. Next week, prompt Emergent to swap in new pairs and keep the same scoring.

faq_plan.a: A matching quiz maker turns a list of pairs, such as words and meanings or pictures and names, into a quiz where each item is matched to its partner. Emergent builds one from a plain-English prompt, with the scoring and a table that keeps every pick.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up matching quiz maker?
faq_plan.a: Open Emergent's AI survey builder and describe your pairs, who takes the quiz, and what counts as a pass. Emergent builds the questions, the scoring, and the database behind them. Change any of it by prompt, then share the link.

faq_plan.q: Is there a free matching quiz maker that saves every answer?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing a matching quiz. Each answer is stored with the partner the person chose, in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I use a vocab matching quiz maker for each week's new terms?
faq_plan.a: Paste the week's words with their meanings and ask for one question per word, with the other meanings as the wrong choices. Next week, prompt for the new list and keep the scoring. To test meanings one word at a time instead of in pairs, build a vocabulary quiz.

faq_plan.q: What makes a good question in a matching type quiz maker?
faq_plan.a: A good matching question has exactly one partner that fits and wrong choices of the same kind. Read each pair aloud before you publish: if a second partner could fit, rewrite one of them.

faq_plan.q: Should a vocabulary matching quiz maker show the term or the definition first?
faq_plan.a: Show the term first for a new list, and students only have to recognize each meaning. Once the class knows the list, flip it: show the definition first and ask them to recall the term.

faq_plan.q: Can a free online matching quiz maker work for staff training?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Pair each rule, term, or product feature with its partner, set a pass mark, and send a retake link to anyone under it. For a quiz on workplace rules with a pass mark, start from a compliance quiz.

faq_plan.q: How is a match up quiz maker different from a multiple choice quiz?
faq_plan.a: A match-up quiz asks people to pair items from two lists, while a multiple-choice quiz asks single questions with one right answer each. On a phone, a match-up set can show one item per screen with its possible partners as the choices, as the quiz on this page does.

faq_plan.q: How do I run a mix and match quiz maker game at an office party?
faq_plan.a: Collect one short fact from each coworker a week ahead, and leave out anything a person would not want shared. At the party, players match coworkers to facts on their phones. Emergent puts no cap on how many responses the game takes.

faq_plan.q: Can a picture matching quiz maker work for a Sunday school class?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put a picture on each question, such as a drawing of an ark, and ask children to match it to the story it comes from. For questions on verses rather than pictures, build a bible quiz.

quiz.title: Matching Quiz: Pair 8 Baby Animals With Their Names
quiz.intro: Each question pairs an animal with the name for its young, in one direction or the other. Pick one answer per question; your score and the answer key show at the end.

questions.text: A baby kangaroo matches which name?
questions.explanation: The name is shared: a baby koala or a baby opossum is a joey too.

source.quote: A baby kangaroo, koala, and opossum are all known as a joey

questions.text: Which name matches a young deer?
questions.explanation: Fawn is the noun for a young deer, so this pair is deer and fawn.

source.quote: A fawn is a young deer

questions.text: A leveret is the young of which animal?
questions.explanation: A leveret is a young hare, especially one in its first year.

source.quote: a young hare especially one in its first year

questions.text: Which name matches a young goose?
questions.explanation: Duckling and cygnet are close neighbors, which is why this pair is easy to swap.

source.quote: A baby goose is called a gosling

questions.text: A filly is the young female of which animal?
questions.explanation: A filly is a young female horse.

source.quote: A filly is a young female horse

questions.text: An eyas is the young of which bird?
questions.explanation: An eyas is a very young hawk or falcon.

source.quote: An eyas is a very young falcon or hawk

questions.text: Which animal's young are called cubs?
questions.explanation: Cub names the young of certain meat eaters, such as the bear, the wolf, and the lion.

source.quote: the young of certain carnivorous mammals such as the bear or wolf or lion

questions.text: A tadpole grows up to be which animal?
questions.explanation: A tadpole is a baby frog, so the pair is tadpole and frog.

source.quote: A tadpole is basically a baby frog

results.title: Keep Matching
results.description: A few pairs got crossed. Open the answer key to see the name you picked beside the right one; that wrong pick is the most useful line in any matching quiz.

results.title: A Good Eye for Pairs
results.description: You matched most of the set. The pairs you missed are listed in the answer key with the name you chose, so you can see which two names you swapped.

results.title: Matching Pro
results.description: You paired almost every animal with its young. Try the set on a friend and compare which names each of you swapped.
